claim.quote: for oxygen-nucleus collisions at incident energies of 60 and 200 GeV per nucleon for Al, Ag, and W target nuclei

name: HELIOS transverse-energy distributions in oxygen-nucleus collisions

summary.plain: HELIOS measured how much transverse energy comes out of collisions of 60 and 200 GeV per nucleon oxygen nuclei with aluminium, silver and tungsten targets, over five orders of magnitude in cross-section, and used it to estimate the energy density reached.
summary.technical: Transverse-energy distributions in -0.1 < eta_lab < 2.9 for 16O-nucleus collisions (Al, Ag, W targets) at 60 and 200 GeV/nucleon, measured over 5 orders of magnitude in cross-section to ET of 200 GeV; dET/deta as a function of eta; for central collisions ET in this region scales roughly as A^0.5; compared with a dual parton model; the energy density is addressed.

title: The transverse energy distribution in 16O-nucleus collisions at 60 and 200 GeV per nucleon
why_it_matters: One of the first transverse-energy measurements with ion beams at the SPS; a 1991 review of HELIOS results states the energy density reached is in the region of the lattice-QCD critical value (2.5 GeV/fm3) for deconfinement.
